name: Dapagliflozin
summary: An SGLT2 inhibitor that lowers glucose via urinary excretion and delivers heart-failure and CKD benefits independent of diabetes status.
mechanism: Blocks SGLT2 in the proximal tubule, reducing glucose and sodium reabsorption and increasing urinary glucose excretion.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers A1c, promotes mild weight loss and natriuresis; improves heart failure outcomes and slows CKD progression independent of glycemia.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Glycosuria within hours of first dose

dosing.adult: 10 mg once daily, morning, with or without food

contraindications: Dialysis or eGFR below initiation threshold (e.g., <25 mL/min/1.73 m2)
warnings: Volume depletion and hypotension, especially with diuretics
Rare euglycemic ketoacidosis — hold before major surgery
safety.overdose: Volume depletion; supportive care. Hypoglycemia unlikely alone

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Chronic kidney disease with or without diabetes
clinicalPearls: DAPA-HF and DAPA-CKD showed benefit regardless of diabetes — indication is not limited to glycemic control.
Hold the drug around surgery or serious illness to reduce euglycemic DKA risk.
good: Cardio-renal benefit in HFrEF and CKD; weight-losing, low-hypoglycemia profile.
bad: Recurrent genital infections, dehydration-prone states, or patients who cannot hold it perioperatively.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard endocrinology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
